4a(1).fact: Sensors provide minute electrical signals that drive transistor switches or electromechanical relays, which in turn manage the heavy current loads demanded by external hardware.
4a(1).misconception: A sensor like a photocell or thermistor directly supplies the heavy electrical current required to power large output devices like motors or high wattage lamps.
4a(1).pamphlet_summary: Control circuits monitor physical environmental inputs through sensors like thermistors or photoresistors to regulate an output device such as a relay, motor, or heating element. A small control signal switches or adjusts a much larger electrical load to automate mechanical tasks safely (p. 42).
4a(1).socratic_question: How can a tiny sensor detecting changes in room temperature safely switch on a heavy air conditioner without burning out?

4a(2).fact: Digital logic circuits categorize input voltages strictly into two distinct high or low binary states representing true or false.
4a(2).misconception: Digital circuits measure continuously varying voltage levels along a smooth infinite spectrum to determine numerical values.
4a(2).pamphlet_summary: Digital logic processes information using two distinct voltage states representing binary one and binary zero to perform deterministic decisions. Fundamental logic gates including AND, OR, and NOT combine binary inputs according to strict mathematical rules defined on truth tables (p. 50).
4a(2).socratic_question: Why do digital computers rely exclusively on two discrete voltage states instead of measuring every possible voltage level in between?

4a(3).fact: Analog systems manipulate continuously varying electrical waveforms directly through linear amplification and passive frequency filtering without any digital conversion.
4a(3).misconception: Analog circuits must convert environmental sound and temperature signals into binary numbers before they can boost or filter them.
4a(3).pamphlet_summary: Analog circuits continuously manipulate smoothly varying physical quantities to achieve amplification, audio reproduction, and radio frequency modulation. Components like operational amplifiers and tuned filter networks process these proportional electrical signals without converting them into numerical steps (p. 36).
4a(3).socratic_question: What happens to the electrical wave generated by a microphone as it travels through an analog guitar amplifier to a loudspeaker?

4c(1).fact: A solid state control project uses active semiconductor devices such as transistors or integrated circuits to automate switching in response to environmental sensor changes.
4c(1).misconception: Electronic control devices operate purely on mechanical contact switches without using semiconductor components to trigger output responses.
4c(1).pamphlet_summary: Building a control device project involves assembling an input sensor network that drives a switching transistor or relay to govern an output. The project must be carefully soldered or wire wrapped on a circuit board and tested under varying environmental conditions to verify dependable switching (p. 61).
4c(1).socratic_question: When you build an automatic nightlight project, how does the circuit decide exactly when room darkness requires turning on the indicator lamp?

4c(2).fact: Floating inputs on digital integrated circuits pick up ambient electrical noise and cause unpredictable erratic outputs unless tied to ground or supply voltage through pull resistors.
4c(2).misconception: Unconnected logic gate input pins on a digital integrated circuit automatically default to a reliable low or off state during operation.
4c(2).pamphlet_summary: Constructing a digital circuit involves wiring integrated circuit chips, logic gates, or pulse generating timers to manipulate discrete binary states. Builders must ensure proper power decoupling and follow pinout diagrams carefully to prevent floating inputs from causing spurious logic transitions (p. 68).
4c(2).socratic_question: If you are assembling a digital counter kit, what might cause the readout display to skip numbers rapidly when you touch the circuit board?

4c(3).fact: Electrolytic capacitors commonly found in analog power and audio circuits are polarized components that can fail or short circuit if installed backwards.
4c(3).misconception: Orientation does not matter when installing capacitors into an analog circuit project because all capacitors conduct current identically in either direction.
4c(3).pamphlet_summary: Assembling an analog circuit project requires connecting discrete components such as resistors, capacitors, and transistors to shape continuous waveforms. Careful component placement and clean solder joints minimize stray capacitance, parasitic oscillation, and unwanted acoustic hum in sensitive audio stages (p. 76).
4c(3).socratic_question: Why can a messy solder joint or misplaced lead introduce a loud buzzing hum into an audio amplifier project?
